title: Routing & Auth Interlock — tactical field notes
content:
Context: quick interlock between control-plane, routing and auth squads to reconcile quota-decay experiment, canary fallback policy, and the rolling key rotation that starts next week. Meeting was 30 minutes; notes capture decisions, open questions, and action items.

Attendees:
- Lena Morales (notes)
- Marcus Nguyen
- Priya Shah
- Tomás Alvarez
- Riley Park
- Optional: Jae Kim (observability pinged in chat)

Topline summary:
- Quota-decay prototype (PLTFM-2592) showed expected drop in tail latency when decay window is 90s, but some customers with bursty patterns see premature throttling.
- Canary for auth key rotation scheduled 2027-10-27; need a short lived safety-net fallback to previous keyset for 30m if 5xx>1% in 10m window.
- Routing fallback policy (cost-first tier) caused a regression in a routing rule that slices by region; we will patch with a fast guardrail and open a PR for a more general policy admission check.

Notes + observations:
- Quota-decay experiment details:
  * Decay window: 90s (baseline was 300s).
  * Observed 12% reduction in median token-cost for steady workloads, ~18% reduction p50 latency.
  * Spike handling: customers with 30s inter-request intervals got rate-limited earlier than before. We expect this to be parameterizable per route.
  * Logs: see sample trace PLTFM-2592-EX1 (linked in Jira).
- Auth key rotation:
  * Rotation flow: control-plane issues new keyset -> clients fetch via public JWKS -> servers validate.
  * Risk vector: clients that cache JWKS aggressively may fail to pick up new key for >2m.
  * Mitigation: publish a short TTL advisory on JWKS endpoint and push coordination note to SRE channel 24h prior to rotation.
- Routing fallback regression:
  * Repro steps captured by Tomás: route-selector matched fallback tier when GPU pool temporarily reported 0 capacity; the fallback applied cost-tier enforcement but lost the region affinity tag causing additional cross-region hops.
  * Immediate patch: prevent fallback from removing region-affinity label (PR #834 opened by Marcus).

Metrics snapshot (from morning query):
- Control-plane qps (global): 4.8k rps
- Auth token validation 50/95/99p latencies: 12ms / 34ms / 160ms
- Quota throttle rate (experiment route): 0.9% -> 1.7% (after decay window change)
- Canary error rate threshold for rollback: 1% 5xx over 10m window (agreed)

Decisions made:
1) Quota-decay will be enabled behind a route-level flag for three customer segments: internal dev, beta customers, GA. Default remains GA-off for now. Rationale: reduce customer-impact blast radius. (Owner: Priya, due: 2027-10-25)
2) Canary rotation safety-net: implement a short-lived fallback that automatically reverts keyset if 5xx>1% in any 10m sliding window during a rotation. Add telemetry hook to surface false positives. (Owner: Marcus, due: 2027-10-26)
3) Immediate routing guard: merge PR that preserves region-affinity label on fallback; follow up with a policy admission check to validate that fallbacks cannot strip required labels. (Owner: Marcus -> PR open, Owner2: Tomás for admission check, due: 2027-11-03)

Action items (concrete):
- Priya: add route-level flag config and a short doc on how to opt routes into quota-decay experiment; include example rollout strategy and metrics to watch. (2027-10-25)
- Marcus: implement safety-net rollback for auth rotation and add an alert that surfaces a rotation rollback event in #platform-ops. (2027-10-26)
- Tomás: add admission unit tests for fallback policies and start a small canary run for the admission check in staging. (2027-10-28)
- Riley: update the JWKS endpoint with advisory headers and draft the customer-facing note for rotations; coordinate with comms. (2027-10-24)
- Lena: collect 3 example customer traces that hit the quota-decay throttle too early; put them in PLTFM-2592 comments. (2027-10-22)

Open questions / risks:
- Is 90s decay window the right default for medium-burst customers? Could we set adaptive decay based on route traffic pattern? (Priya to prototype adaptive decay in spike detector.)
- How noisy will the rotation safety-net be for environments with flaky network? We need to tune the alerting to avoid unnecessary rollbacks. (Marcus to propose tuning plan.)
- Multi-region routing: do we need a stricter policy that prevents cross-region fallback for latency-sensitive routes? (Action: product to flag routes that must preserve locality.)

Quick follow-ups (notes to self):
- Add a short checklist for rotation to the internal runbook: preflight logs, JWKS TTL advisory, staged rollouts, safety-net thresholds, and post-rotation smoke.
- Consider a lightweight simulation harness to model quota-decay tradeoffs with synthetic bursty workloads. Could be a short spike-generator job in staging.

Links & traces referenced in meeting:
- Jira: PLTFM-2592 (quota-decay), PLTFM-2634 (rotation safety-net)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/834
- Slack thread: #platform-routing (ref Zp3k8xQp)

Next sync: quick midweek check (15m) if any action items land as failing; otherwise full interlock next week same slot.

Notes style: rough — this is a working doc. If anything here should be elevated to Confluence or an RFC, call it out.

End of notes.
